activation.note: Triggers cover pre-ratification attempts, system-owned authoring after confirmation, and changes to the session guard. Task terms and paths are explicitly heuristic; lock-state and caller observations honestly require new observers. Exclusions remain limited to non-authoring conversation and work outside the plan-session flow.

audit.summary: All segments survive in the claimed destinations, including the first-statement guard, exception type, system ownership and complete, atomic, idempotently replayable authoring. The shared node contains generic strict-disposition policy rather than rule-specific behavior; no undeclared coder-facing additions or waivers were found.

segmentChecks.note: The then clause preserves the prohibition on authoring before operator confirmation and locking.
The Ratify boundary, system-not-agent ownership, ratification timing, and per-locked-unit invocation are retained across given, why, prefer[0], and avoid[0].
verifier_detail[0] retains the normative refusal requirement essentially verbatim, and avoid[1] restates the unlocked-writer prohibition.
The false-lock condition, SessionGateError, PlanSession.author(), and ordering before any writer call are all explicit.
The requirement that the lock guard be the first statement is explicit in prefer[1], avoid[1], and verifier_detail[1].
Strict disposition remains explicit in identity and verifier_detail[2]. The shared node only generalizes strict-policy handling and does not replace the rule-specific trace.
System-owned authoring on confirm is preserved per locked unit, including complete, atomic, and idempotently replayable behavior.

risks: The given clause is framed only around the pre-ratification state even though prefer and avoid also impose post-ratification behavior; the explicit phrases 'On ratification' and 'before or after ratification' substantially mitigate this scope ambiguity.

unobservable: phase: current plan-session phase and operator-ratified/locked state require a new observer.
operation: writer invocation, caller identity (agent versus atdd plan), and lock state at invocation require a new observer.
The fires condition that the planner is 'tempted' to invoke a writer is a mental/intentional state, not a Datalog-observable fact.
A writer being 'about to be invoked' is prospective and is not observable without a pre-invocation hook.

review.summary: All examined source knowledge is preserved without material distortion, and the coder-facing instructions clearly distinguish agent behavior from system-owned authoring. Activation is not currently deterministic because session, caller, and prospective-invocation facts need instrumentation, but those observer gaps are disclosed and do not change the preservation verdict.
